=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): opposite (clearly visible paired leaves attached at the same node along the stem in multiple views)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (leaves are grouped closely together at the apex of the shoot system)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): compound (each leaf unit is divided into multiple distinct leaflets)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): odd-pinnate (each leaf has a terminal leaflet at the apex of the rachis)
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): 5 (consistently observed five leaflets per leaf in all images)
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): alternate (leaflets are attached at different points along the rachis, not strictly in pairs)
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.): entire (leaf edges are smooth without teeth or serrations)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): ovate (leaflets are broadly egg-shaped, widest below the middle)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (leaf tips taper to a distinct point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): rounded (leaf bases are generally circular or blunt)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with veins branching off to the sides)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): clearly visible, spaced regularly, numerous
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): glabrous (surfaces appear smooth and hairless)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on leaf surfaces)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles connecting leaflets to the rachis are visibly brief)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (petioles appear rounded in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): herbaceous (stem appears green, soft, and non-woody)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem surface appears smooth)
    19. Stem color: green
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no visible ridges, lenticels, or roughness)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): absent (no stipules visible at leaf nodes)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no visible swelling at the base of the leaflets or petioles)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils are visible)
F. Notes: One of the lower leaflets exhibits a distinct hole in the leaf blade.
